preconditions.description: Attacker must have owner role on the contract

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, exploit the centralized privileges by: 1) Call issue() to mint new tokens to owner address, increasing attacker balance. 2) Call setParams() to increase basisPointsRate and maximumFee to extract fees from all transfers. 3) Call addBlackList() on target users followed by destroyBlackFunds() to confiscate their tokens. 4) Call deprecate() to redirect all token operations to a malicious upgraded contract. The owner has unrestricted control over token supply, user funds, and contract behavior.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: This is a classic Owner Privilege Abuse vulnerability in the TetherToken contract. The owner has unrestricted control over: 1) Token supply via issue() function that mints new tokens to owner, 2) Transfer fees via setParams(), 3) User funds via blacklist/destroy functions, 4) Contract behavior via deprecate(). The oracle checks if attacker_balance_increased, so the simplest exploit is to become owner and call issue() to mint tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1) Use vm.store() to overwrite the owner storage slot (slot 0) with attacker address, 2) Call issue() to mint new tokens to attacker, 3) Verify balance increased. This is the most direct path to satisfy the oracle check.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Define ITetherToken interface with issue() and balanceOf() functions, 2. In setUp(), use vm.store() to set attacker as owner at slot 0, 3. In testExploit(), call issue() to mint tokens, 4. Assert balance increased using assertGt()
